problem_statement: thekamalkashyap/blogging-website-template is the Techipedia blog: a Next.js 12 + Tailwind + MDX editorial starter with a shared LayoutWrapper header/footer, a data-driven nav (data/headerNavLinks.js -> Blogs / Tags / Reading Guide / About / Source Code), a paginated post list (layouts/ListLayout.js rendering article cards), tag routes, an author About page, and MDX posts under data/blog. New readers land on a flat reverse-chronological list with no guided entry point. Add a cross-page Reading Guide experience that groups the existing posts into curated learning tracks: (1) a native /reading-guide page built from the site's own design system (shared LayoutWrapper shell, the page-title heading rhythm, and article cards mirroring ListLayout) with a Learning Tracks section; (2) an interactive level filter on that page - a row of level chips (All / Beginner / Intermediate / Advanced) that filters the visible track cards, with a live '#track-readout' label that always reflects the current selection (e.g. 'Showing 1 track - Advanced'); (3) a shared 'Continue your reading path' Reading Rail component that surfaces the top tracks as a chip row and is wired onto every browse surface (the home list, the Tags index, and the Reading Guide page) through a single surface whitelist, so the reading-path cadence is consistent across the site. The rail chip row must wrap fluidly and stay within the viewport at 390px, and must keep the calm Techipedia palette (white/neutral cards, dodger-blue accents) rather than an off-system restyle. Do not fork a bespoke standalone page or invent a new visual language; the Reading Guide and rail must feel like a first-class part of Techipedia. Ground the work in the repo's own assets and shared Tailwind visual state rather than introducing external stock media.
required_content: A new /reading-guide route renders a Reading Guide page built from the shared Techipedia shell (SectionContainer/LayoutWrapper header + footer), a page-title heading, and a Learning Tracks section.

The Reading Guide lists several curated learning tracks, each rendered as an article card with its own heading (matching the ListLayout card heading rhythm) and a descriptive summary paragraph grouping existing posts.
The 'Reading Guide' entry is registered in the shared navigation (data/headerNavLinks.js) so the nav link renders in the header on the home list AND on the Reading Guide page itself.
The Reading Guide reuses the existing design language - Tailwind type scale, spacing, dark-mode colors, and rounded card treatment - rather than a bespoke inline-styled layout.
Existing routes (home list, tags, tag detail, about, MDX posts) and the shared header/footer navigation remain reachable and unchanged in behavior.
Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile renders of the Reading Guide and the home list have no horizontal overflow and no console/network errors.

Existing local image assets under public/static/images (e.g. the author and post images loaded via the Next.js Image component on the About and image-guide post) keep loading without 404s across the captured states.

The Reading Guide page renders an interactive level filter: a chip row (All / Beginner / Intermediate / Advanced) that filters the visible track cards, and a live '#track-readout' label that always reflects the current selection (clicking 'Advanced' updates it to 'Showing 1 track - Advanced', not a stale initial value). Each level chip is a clickable control that carries a `data-level-filter` attribute set to its level name (`data-level-filter="All"` / `"Beginner"` / `"Intermediate"` / `"Advanced"`) so the active selection is programmatically addressable, and the readout element uses the id `track-readout`.

A shared 'Continue your reading path' Reading Rail (a chip row of the top learning tracks) renders on the home list AND the Tags index AND the Reading Guide page, controlled by a single surface whitelist, so the cross-page reading-path cadence is present on every browse surface.

The Reading Rail chip row wraps fluidly and produces no horizontal overflow at 390px on any surface, and its chips keep the Techipedia card palette (white/neutral surface, dodger-blue accents) rather than an off-system saturated restyle.
design_constraints: Preserve Techipedia's design language: Tailwind utility rhythm, the page-title heading scale used by Tags/List layouts, generous whitespace, dark-mode palette, and the shared SectionContainer max-width column.
Reuse the existing card pattern from layouts/ListLayout.js (an article with a heading + summary paragraph) for each learning track instead of inventing a new component style.
Register the new section in the shared data/headerNavLinks.js so the header nav (desktop and MobileNav) renders it on every page; do not hard-code a one-off link on a single page.
Do not turn the page into a dashboard, marketing landing page, or a bespoke standalone 'cheatsheet' with inline styles that ignore the site theme.
Keep the Next.js content model intact: the new page is a static Next.js page under pages/, and post/tag/about routes keep building.

The level filter and its readout must stay in sync on every interaction: derive the readout from the live selected level on each render (do not freeze it in a mount-only closure). Tag each level chip with a `data-level-filter` attribute equal to its level label (All/Beginner/Intermediate/Advanced) and give the live readout element the id `track-readout`, so the current selection is addressable and the chosen level's readout can be verified.
Control the Reading Rail's cross-page presence from one shared surface whitelist so it appears on all browse surfaces at once, not hard-coded per page and not omitted from secondary pages.
Keep the Reading Rail chip row responsive (wrap on narrow viewports) and on-palette; do not ship a fixed-width nowrap row that overflows mobile or an off-system color restyle.
state_constraints: desktop_initial/tablet_initial/mobile_initial capture the Techipedia home list with the shared header nav; without the task the nav has no Reading Guide entry.
desktop_search_next captures the paginated blog list route (/blog/page/1) to confirm existing listing routes stay intact.
desktop_tags and mobile_tags capture the Tags index; desktop_tag_next captures a tag detail route.
desktop_about captures the author About page; desktop_post_code and desktop_post_images capture two MDX post routes.

desktop_reading_guide_route and mobile_reading_guide_route capture the new /reading-guide route: present and consistent in the reference, a real 404 in the baseline (route does not exist), and an off-system standalone page in the bad solution.

Source inspection confirms the shared nav is data-driven via data/headerNavLinks.js and the post list cards come from layouts/ListLayout.js, so the Reading Guide can be built from the same design system.

desktop_home_rail and mobile_home_rail scroll the shared Reading Rail into view on the home list; the reference rail wraps within the viewport and keeps the Techipedia palette, while the baseline/bad rail is a fixed-width nowrap off-palette row that overflows the 390px mobile viewport.

desktop_guide_prefilter captures the Reading Guide with the default 'All' level selected (readout 'Showing 6 tracks - All levels'); desktop_guide_filtered clicks the 'Advanced' level chip - the reference/baseline readout updates to 'Showing 1 track - Advanced', while a stale-closure bad solution leaves it frozen.

change_completion: A /reading-guide page renders with the Reading Guide title, a Learning Tracks section, and named curated tracks (e.g. Next.js Foundations, Tailwind CSS, Build/SEO/Deploy).
The 'Reading Guide' nav link is registered and renders in the shared header on both the home list and the Reading Guide page.
Existing home/tags/tag/about/post routes and the shared header/footer remain reachable.
design_consistency: The Reading Guide reuses the shared SectionContainer shell, the page-title heading scale, and ListLayout-style article cards (heading + summary) rather than a bespoke inline-styled layout.
Typography, spacing, dark-mode palette, and card treatment match the rest of Techipedia.
The section is registered cross-page in the shared nav rather than as a one-off hard-coded link.
regression: All existing routes still build and serve; the shared nav still lists Blogs/Tags/About.
No console or network errors are introduced on any captured state.
responsive: 390px mobile and tablet renders of the Reading Guide and home list have no horizontal overflow.
The track cards and header nav wrap cleanly on mobile.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Next.js + Tailwind + MDX design_continuity ADD/cross_page task. The Techipedia starter exposes a data-driven shared nav (data/headerNavLinks.js) and a reusable article-card list (layouts/ListLayout.js), so the natural extension is a new /reading-guide page built from the same design system and registered in the shared nav so its link renders on every page. Baseline lacks the page (route 404s) and the nav entry; a known-bad off-system standalone 'Reading Cheatsheet' page uses inline styles, no shared cards, and is never registered - it fails completion, visible-text, forbidden-pattern (Cheatsheet), and DOM assertions. Runability passes via next build + next start; all twelve states capture clean in the reference.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: tailwind-nextjs-starter-blog (Techipedia) Next.js + Tailwind + MDX editorial blog with a data-driven shared nav and reusable article-card list; design_continuity page ADD introducing a cross-page Reading Guide section built from the shared design system and registered nav while preserving existing editorial routes and visual rhythm.
